description: Municipality geo ID (BO-DD-PP-MM) in the GADM 4.1 hierarchy of the 339-unit municipality map. It nests by prefix into the department (BO-DD) and province (BO-DD-PP) IDs; department and province numbers follow GADM order and differ from INE codes.
Calendar year of the estimate (2001–2020).
ID (AidData asdf_id) of the geoBoundaries v4 ADM3 polygon on which DS4Bolivia computed the data, matched one-to-one to the GADM municipality by area overlap.
source: DS4Bolivia

description: Estimated number of people living in the municipality: the sum over its polygon of the WorldPop unconstrained global population mosaic at 1 km (aggregated from 100 m random-forest dasymetric estimates; not UN-adjusted), extracted with AidData GeoQuery. Gridded estimates, not INE's official projections.
source: WorldPop via DS4Bolivia

description: Population (pop) divided by the municipality's area in km², measured on its GADM 4.1 boundary in the project's equal-area projection (an Albers projection fitted to Bolivia).
source: WorldPop via DS4Bolivia; areas from GADM 4.1 boundaries

description: Municipality geo ID (BO-DD-PP-MM) in the GADM 4.1 hierarchy of the 339-unit municipality map. It nests by prefix into the department (BO-DD) and province (BO-DD-PP) IDs; department and province numbers follow GADM order and differ from INE codes.
Calendar year of the observation (2012–2020). The 2012 lights composite covers April 2012 to March 2013.
ID (AidData asdf_id) of the geoBoundaries v4 ADM3 polygon on which DS4Bolivia computed the data, matched one-to-one to the GADM municipality by area overlap.
source: DS4Bolivia

description: Natural log of night-time radiance per person, ln(10⁸ × NTL / population). NTL is the sum over the municipality of the EOG Annual VIIRS Nighttime Lights V2 average radiance (background masked, 15 arc-seconds, nW/cm²/sr), extracted with AidData GeoQuery; population is the same year's WorldPop 1 km sum. Missing where no pixel remained lit after masking (2–15 municipalities a year).
source: EOG VIIRS nighttime lights and WorldPop, via DS4Bolivia

description: Hodrick–Prescott trend (λ = 400) of the log of night-time lights per capita. The log of lights, gap-filled within each municipality by linear interpolation and extrapolation (and a fixed-effects prediction where needed), and the log of population are each HP-filtered and combined as ln(10⁸ × trend NTL / trend population). Complete for every municipality and year, including years where ln_NTLpc is missing.
source: EOG VIIRS nighttime lights and WorldPop, via DS4Bolivia

description: GDO-Bolivia geo ID of the municipality (BO-DD-PP-MM), following the GADM 4.1 hierarchy of the 339-unit municipality map; department and province numbers follow GADM order and differ from INE codes. Nests by prefix into the department (BO-DD) and province (BO-DD-PP) IDs.

Reference year of the indicator values in the row. Each SDG Atlas indicator is stored only at its own reference year (geo:year); indicators averaged over a period are stored at the period's midpoint, rounded down, so the panel is sparse.

Official municipality code of the National Statistics Institute (INE), DDPPMM (department, province, municipality) stored as an integer without the leading zero (e.g. 20101 = La Paz). The Atlas indicators are linked to geo_id through this code, which places DS4Bolivia's three swapped homonym pairs in their correct municipality.
source: INE via DS4Bolivia

description: Estimated municipal population in 2020 (persons), as shown in the Atlas municipal profiles ("Población estimada, 2020"). The Atlas does not state the source of the estimate; it is presumably INE's municipal population projections, which the Atlas uses as denominators elsewhere. Differs from the gridded WorldPop-based `pop` dataset.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Share of the municipal population living in urban areas in 2012 (%), from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE). INE counts as urban the localities with 2,000 or more inhabitants, which is why 175 municipalities have a rate of 0.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of dwellings that consumed less than 25% of the Tarifa Dignidad (subsidised tariff) limit, i.e. under 210 kWh per year, in May 2016; dwellings without electricity (and thus without a meter) also count as extremely energy poor. Built by Andersen, Branisa & Calderón (2019), from residential electricity-meter records.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of the population with Unsatisfied Basic Needs (NBI) in 2012, the official INE poverty measure covering housing, energy, education and health deprivations, computed from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Alkire-Foster multidimensional poverty index (0-1) with 9 deprivation indicators (e.g. illiterate member, child aged 6-19 not studying, no drinking water, no electricity, no sanitation, no phone, birth outside a health centre, teen pregnancy, member without ID), computed from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE) with the INESAD/Swisscontact methodology of Andersen & Branisa (2020).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of households with access to all three basic services (electricity, water and sanitation) in 2012, from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of children under 5 with chronic malnutrition in 2016. The 2016 Demographic and Health Survey (EDSA, INE and Ministry of Health; table 24) is not representative by municipality, so the Atlas assigns each municipality the rate of its department and poverty level (high, medium or low).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of women aged 15-49 (not pregnant and without a birth in the two months before the survey) with obesity (BMI >= 30) in 2016, imputed to municipalities from the 2016 Demographic and Health Survey (table 28) by department and poverty level.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Average area per Agricultural Production Unit (UPA) in hectares, from the 2013 Agricultural Census (INE). Not applicable (missing) for the 15 municipalities that are 95% or more urban.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Number of tractors per 1,000 Agricultural Production Units (UPAs), from the 2013 Agricultural Census (INE). Not applicable (missing) for the 15 almost fully urban municipalities.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of births attended in a health facility, average of 2008-2012, the official INE indicator computed from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE). Stored at 2010.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Infant mortality rate: deaths of children before their first birthday per 1,000 live births, 2016; official municipal estimates by UDAPE (2018).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Under-five mortality rate: deaths of children before age 5 per 1,000 live births, 2016; official municipal estimates by UDAPE (2018).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Chagas (vector) infestation rate: percentage of dwellings infested, 2017, from the National Chagas Programme of the Ministry of Health (data via the National Health Information System, SNIS).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Dengue cases per 10,000 inhabitants in 2018, from the National Dengue-Chikungunya-Zika Control and Prevention Programme of the Ministry of Health (SNIS).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Annual malaria cases per 1,000 inhabitants, average of 2014-2017, from the National Malaria Programme of the Ministry of Health (SNIS). Stored at 2015.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Incidence of tuberculosis in all its forms (new cases and relapses) per 100,000 inhabitants in 2017, from the National Tuberculosis Programme of the Ministry of Health (SNIS).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Annual new HIV cases per 1,000,000 inhabitants, average of 2014-2017 (averaged because cases are few), from the National STI/HIV/AIDS and Viral Hepatitis Programme of the Ministry of Health (SNIS). Stored at 2015.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Births per 1,000 women aged 15–19, average of 2008–2012 (stored at 2010, the midpoint), computed from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE) as described in Branisa et al. (2016).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Secondary-school dropout rate of male students in 2017: dropouts divided by enrolment (%), official administrative data from the Ministry of Education's Educational Statistics and Indicators System (SEIE, seie.minedu.gob.bo).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Secondary-school dropout rate of female students in 2017: dropouts divided by enrolment (%), official administrative data from the Ministry of Education's Educational Statistics and Indicators System (SEIE, seie.minedu.gob.bo).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of the population aged 19 or older that has reached higher (tertiary) education, 2012, official INE indicator from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Literacy rate of people aged 15 or older, 2012, official INE indicator from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of qualified teachers at the initial (pre-primary) level, 2016, from the Ministry of Education's Educational Statistics and Indicators System (SEIE, seie.minedu.gob.bo). The Atlas does not define 'qualified'.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of qualified teachers at the secondary level, 2016, from the Ministry of Education's Educational Statistics and Indicators System (SEIE, seie.minedu.gob.bo). The Atlas does not define 'qualified'.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Gender parity index of secondary-school dropout, 2017, from the Ministry of Education's Educational Statistics and Indicators System (SEIE, seie.minedu.gob.bo). The Atlas gives no formula; the values (0-7, median 1.4) track the ratio of the male to the female dropout rate, so values of 1 or more mean girls drop out no more than boys (the Atlas target is 1).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Gender parity index in years of education of young people aged 25-35, 2012: years of schooling of women relative to men (1 = parity; values below 1 mean women have fewer years). Atlas calculation from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Gender parity index in the multidimensional poverty index by sex of the household head, 2012 (Andersen & Branisa, 2020), from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE); it shows whether female-headed households are more likely to be poor than male-headed ones. Values below 1 indicate that female-headed households are worse off (the Atlas target is 1); the exact ratio is not stated.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Ratio of the female to the male global labour-force participation rate (population aged 10 or older that works, with or without pay, or seeks work), 2012, from two official INE rates computed with the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of the population with drinking-water coverage in 2017, unpublished official data provided by the Vice-Ministry of Drinking Water and Basic Sanitation; the Atlas has no details on its methodology.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of the population with sanitation coverage in 2017, unpublished official data provided by the Vice-Ministry of Drinking Water and Basic Sanitation; the Atlas has no details on its methodology.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Proportion of wastewater that is treated, 2017, from the regulator's (AAPS, Ministry of Environment and Water) 2018 performance study of the regulated water and sewerage providers (EPSAs). Six municipalities have values above 100 in the source data.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of the population with electricity coverage in 2012, official INE indicator from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Residential electricity consumption per capita in 2016 (kWh per person per year): total residential electricity consumed in the municipality divided by INE's 2016 population estimate. From Andersen, Branisa & Calderón (2019), from residential electricity-meter records.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of households that cook with clean energy (electricity, piped natural gas or LPG cylinders), 2012, Atlas calculation from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Energy-related CO2 emissions per capita in 2016 (tCO2 per person per year): municipal consumption of diesel, gasoline, electricity and LPG multiplied by the CO2 emission factor of each energy type, divided by population. From Andersen, Branisa & Calderón (2019).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of residential electricity meters that recorded zero consumption in May 2016, a proxy for infrastructure left unused part of the year (inefficient use of resources). From Andersen, Branisa & Calderón (2019), from residential electricity-meter records.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Global participation rate of men aged 10 or older: share economically active (working, with or without pay, or seeking work), 2012, official INE indicator from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Global participation rate of women aged 10 or older: share economically active (working, with or without pay, or seeking work), 2012, official INE indicator from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

varlabel: Young men not studying or active (%)
description: Percentage of young men aged 15-24 who neither study nor participate in the labour market ('NINIs'), 2012, Atlas calculation from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

varlabel: Young women not studying or active (%)
description: Percentage of young women aged 15-24 who neither study nor participate in the labour market ('NINIs'), 2012, Atlas calculation from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Number of commercial bank branches per 100,000 inhabitants in 2018, from the Financial System Supervisory Authority (ASFI) and INE population projections.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Index of migratory intermediation (IIM), 2012: betweenness centrality of the municipality in the network of internal migration flows between municipalities, normalised by the theoretical maximum, i.e. how often it lies on the shortest migration paths between other pairs of municipalities (Rocha-Portugal, Vera-Cossío & Wanderley, 2020, IISEC-UCB). The paper defines it on 0-1; the stored values (0-15.1) appear to be scaled by 100.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Number of railways and primary roads (Red Fundamental, the national trunk network) entering or leaving the municipality, 2019, computed by Conservación Internacional Bolivia from the 2019 Red Fundamental map. Ranges from 0 (85 unconnected municipalities) to 6.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Kuaa laptops (made by a state company and delivered to public-school students) per 100 school-age inhabitants aged 6-19, stock at end of 2016, from AGETIC (2018).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of (public) educational units with 'pisos tecnológicos' (technology classrooms/equipment), 2016, from AGETIC (2018).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of households with a fixed or mobile telephone, 2012, official INE indicator from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE). It measures household phone access, not network coverage.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Number of mobile radio base stations (which carry the signal for mobile internet) per 1,000 inhabitants in 2016, Atlas calculation from AGETIC (2018) data.
unit: number of radio bases per 1,000 inhabitants
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Gini coefficient of years of education of the population aged 25-65, 2012, from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE) (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Generalised entropy index GE(-1), which stresses the bottom of the distribution, of residential electricity consumption per household, 2016. From Andersen, Branisa & Calderón (2019), from residential electricity-meter records. Values (10-304) are on the Atlas's scale (bounds 11-228), apparently multiplied by 100.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of the population aged 3 or older that does not speak Spanish (neither as mother tongue nor as first or second language), 2012, from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of households living in overcrowding (more than 2 persons per room), 2012, Atlas calculation from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of households with no sanitary service, bathroom or latrine, 2012, from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Seats available in collective transport (buses, micros and minibuses registered in the municipal vehicle tax register RUAT, plus cable cars and the PumaKatari, ChikiTiti and Wayna Bus fleets) per 1,000 inhabitants. The Atlas labels it 2017; its definition uses 2017–2019 data.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Municipal climate change vulnerability index (2015) from Conservación Internacional Bolivia's Climate Change Atlas: vulnerability to changes in the water balance under IPCC AR4 climate scenarios, combined with socio-economic and environmental capacity to respond. Higher is more vulnerable (range about 0-3).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Total CO2 emissions per capita in 2016 (tCO2 per person per year): emissions from deforestation (biomass burning, from Conservación Internacional Bolivia) plus emissions from burning natural gas, gasoline and diesel (Andersen, Branisa & Calderón, 2019), divided by population.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Annual deforestation rate, average of 2016-2018, as a percentage of the forest area in 2015, computed by Conservación Internacional Bolivia from satellite data (Hansen et al. 2013, Global Forest Change v1.5). Stored at 2017.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Legally declared protected area (national, departmental and municipal) as a percentage of the municipality's area, 2019, computed by Conservación Internacional Bolivia. Two municipalities slightly exceed 100 in the source data.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Biodiversity loss index due to deforestation, average of 2016-2018: a species disturbance index (Andersen & Ledezma, 2019, with Conservación Internacional Bolivia) that weights deforested habitat by the number of species present there, all species weighted equally. Stored at 2017.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Registered homicides per 100,000 inhabitants per year, average of 2015-2017, prepared by the Bolivian Observatory of Citizen Security and Fight against Drugs (OBSCD) from Bolivian Police statistics (Ministry of Government). Stored at 2016.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Budget execution capacity of the municipal government in 2017: executed budget divided by programmed budget (%), from the Ministry of Economy and Public Finance.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of children under 5 whose birth is registered in the civil registry, 2012, official indicator from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Share of municipal revenues that come from local taxes in 2017 (%), the rest being mainly central-government transfers, from the Ministry of Economy and Public Finance.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Public investment per capita in the municipality in 2017 (bolivianos per person), from Ministry of Economy and Public Finance data. The Atlas does not state which population was used as denominator.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Municipality geo ID (BO-DD-PP-MM) in the GADM 4.1 hierarchy of the 339-unit municipality map. It nests by prefix into the department (BO-DD) and province (BO-DD-PP) IDs; department and province numbers follow GADM order and differ from INE codes.
Year of the satellite embeddings (2017).
ID (AidData asdf_id) of the geoBoundaries v4 ADM3 polygon on which DS4Bolivia computed the data, matched one-to-one to the GADM municipality by area overlap.
